1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves the account solely via `accountForSession(session)` from the authenticated session cookie, with no client-supplied user identifier accepted.

2.why: Identity codes are hashed into the specific pending session and TOTP/backup codes are hashed per-account, so a code cannot authenticate any other user.

3.why: `/api/mfa/activate` only mutates the account MFA record — it neither rotates the current session nor deletes other sessions in the `sessions` map, so pre-existing sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM `EncryptedValue` and backup codes only as SHA-256 peppered hashes (`hashValue`), never plaintext.

5.why: All tokens, secrets, OTPs and recovery codes derive from `crypto.getRandomValues` with unbiased rejection sampling in `secureInt`.

6.why: The session id lives only in a `__Host-` HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict cookie and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used; secrets exist only transiently in JS variables/DOM for the demo.

7.why: Server-side `validEmail`, `validPhone`, `validOtp`, the recovery-code regex, JSON content-type and 10 KB body bounds validate all input; there is no SQL layer at all (in-memory Maps).

8.why: All dynamic values (demo code, manual secret, backup codes) are injected with `textContent`/`createElement`, and `innerHTML` is used only with static literals.

9.why: The app issues no redirects whatsoever and paths are restricted to a hard-coded `allowedPaths` allow-list, so no open-redirect surface exists (though no explicit redirect allow-list is coded).

10.why: `headersFor` sets CSP with `frame-ancestors 'none'`, HSTS with includeSubDomains, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, Referrer-Policy and no-store.

12.why: Server responses are generic and stack traces suppressed, but the client deliberately `console.log`s the identity code, manual TOTP secret, provisioning URI (secret in query string) and all backup codes.

13.why: Identity codes have `identityUsed` single-use flag plus a 5-minute `identityExpiresAt`, TOTP replay is blocked via `lastTotpCounter`, and backup codes are marked `used`.

14.why: Identity, TOTP-activation and recovery-code paths each count failures and set a 10-minute lockout after 5 attempts, returning 429.

15.why: `rotateAuthenticatedSession` issues a new id and CSRF token on successful verification, `getSession` enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
